FAMILY TREE · IN ISPUTNIK.HOME

Your family, branch by branch.
Kept at home, not on a genealogy site.

The people in your family, how they’re related, what happened in their lives, and the photos that go with them — with living relatives kept private, and each branch looked after by the cousin who knows it best.

Get iSputnik ↗See what it does ↓
  • No cloud needed
  • No ads
  • No hidden costs
  • No tracking

WHAT IT DOES

From one name to the whole family.

Build it

Start with a name. Everything else can come later.

  • Only a name needed to add someone
  • Forgiving dates: 1943, May 1943 or 9 May 1943
  • Parents, partners, children and siblings — remarriages and step-children too
  • Add relatives straight from the chart
  • Names in another language, found by either spelling

See it

The family from every angle.

  • An interactive chart centred on anyone
  • Profiles with life events, sources and a life story
  • Families and a timeline
  • A map of births, marriages, events and deaths
  • One person’s places, joined in the order they lived them

Photos and faces

The tree points at your gallery — nothing is copied.

  • Attach any photo from the gallery
  • Link a face, and every photo of that person appears
  • Portraits cut from the gallery, or uploaded
  • The stories each person appears in, on their profile

Share it safely

Everyone can see it. Only the right people can change it.

  • Living relatives’ details kept private from newcomers
  • “You” in the tree for each member
  • Branch editors for the cousin who knows their side
  • GEDCOM import and export — Ancestry, MyHeritage, Gramps
  • A package that moves the whole tree to another server

PRIVATE HERE, SPECIFICALLY

Your family isn’t a dataset.

The general promises hold everywhere. These are the ones that matter most for the family tree.

No genealogy company in the middle

Names, dates, places and portraits live in your own database. No service holds your family tree, and nobody can change the terms on it.

Living relatives stay private

People who don’t edit a branch see a living relative’s name, place in the tree and portrait — no dates, places, events or map pins — unless you let them.

Places looked up at home first

Place suggestions come from an offline list. Search online asks OpenStreetMap only when you press it, and only for the words you typed.

Editors can’t overreach

A branch editor changes the people tagged for them. Deleting people, importing GEDCOM and tagging stay with administrators.

WORKS WITH

The people behind every photo.

Photos & home videoFaces recognised in the gallery bring every photo of a person to their profile. StoriesA person block in a story lists it on their profile — recipes included.

WHAT YOU NEED

The family’s memory, and a backup.

iSputnik.home
The family tree is part of it. There is nothing to scan: type people in, or import a GEDCOM file.
A backup
The tree lives only in the app’s database. Include the database in your backups, or export a GEDCOM file now and then.
Face recognition optional
The isputnik.faces container, to bring every photo of a person to their profile.

QUESTIONS

About the family tree.

More in the Family tree guide.

Can I bring my tree from Ancestry or MyHeritage?

Yes — export a GEDCOM file there and import it here. People, families, events and sources come across; photos aren’t part of GEDCOM, so you attach them again from the gallery.

Who can see living relatives?

Members who don’t edit their branch see only a living relative’s name, place in the tree and portrait, unless an administrator allows them the details.

Can a cousin look after their own side?

Yes. Tag the people in their branch and make them its editor. They can edit and add relatives there, but can’t delete people or import files.

What if I only know the year?

That’s enough. A year-only date stays a year-only date — nothing invents a day for it.
